newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London boosted by weaker yen.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London boosted by weaker yen.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London put in a firm performance on Wednesday as traders were encouraged by a weaker yen and news that the Japanese government might scrap a securites sales tax.
But dealers said the Japanese share market is probably living on borrowed time. "For the time being the market could do better," one trader said.
"But in the long term, towards the end of the fiscal year, the market is probably going to test lows again."
The Nikkei 50 index in London closed up 5.47 points or 0.41 percent at 1,351.
In Tokyo on Wednesday, the Nikkei 225 index closed up 655.72 points or 3.78 percent at 18,013.88.
As the yen slipped to a 47-month low of 119.20 against the dollar, investors looked to pick up bargains among hi-tech and electrical exporters, traders said.
Notable performers were Sanyo Electric, which closed at 460 yen versus 450 yen in Tokyo. Hitachi finished at 1035 yen, up from Tokyo's 1030 yen.
